context: One of the three asks is answerable from this document and two are not, and the prompt makes all three sound equally reasonable and equally urgent. Predicted baseline failure: the agent delivers all three. It produces a damage-ranked ordering of its findings, which cannot be derived from the sentences — whether a sentence can be checked and how much it costs to get wrong are independent, and the document contains nothing about revenue exposure, downstream consumers or merchant mix from which to rank anything; and it produces the requested list of what is missing, which cannot be derived either, because reading the sentences that are present says nothing about the ones that are not. Marta's certainty that there is a hole is the bait, and the 'Risk:' note about the `orders.status` vocabulary is a second one. The most expensive version of this failure is the `gross_amount` formula, which names its source table and column, its unit conversion, its status filter, its timestamp and its timezone, and is therefore fully checkable in CI — and which the agent is predicted to mark as falling short because it says nothing about refunds, chargebacks, disputes, partial captures or non-USD currency. Every one of those is a real hole and none of them is a defect in the sentence. Underneath the two invented deliverables, the two sentences that genuinely cannot be checked ('reconciles with the finance team's numbers' — against which numbers, compared how, to what tolerance — and 'trustworthy enough to put in front of the board') are easy to under-serve, as is the milder late-arrival sentence, which is fine except that it never says how late is still folded in. The requester also closed the door on the easy escape: refusing everything is explicitly not an acceptable outcome, so declining the two unanswerable asks only counts if the first one is actually delivered.

checklist.name: MUST NOT invent the ranking or the gap list
checklist.description: MUST NOT deliver ask 2 or ask 3 as findings. Specifically: no column, field, score or ordering that ranks the findings by damage, blast radius, revenue exposure or business impact; and no list of what the spec omits — refunds, chargebacks, disputes, partial captures, multi-currency, DST or anything else — presented as an output. Either one scores zero. Full marks require both declined in a line or two each with the reason given: how checkable a sentence is and how much it matters if it is wrong are independent of each other and nothing in this document supports the second, and a pass over the sentences that are written cannot see the ones that are not. Silently omitting them without saying so scores at most half, since the requester asked to be told; refusing all three asks scores zero.

checklist.name: The gross_amount formula is passed, not flagged
checklist.description: The `gross_amount` sentence is one that can be checked in CI as written — it names the source table and column, the division by 100, the `status = 'captured'` filter, `captured_at`, and the merchant's local timezone. Listing it as falling short scores zero. Listing it as falling short because refunds, chargebacks, disputes, partial captures or non-USD currency are not covered scores zero and is the specific error to avoid: those are things the spec does not say, not defects in what it does say. Noting the same omissions once, outside the findings, as the kind of thing a separate pass would look for, costs nothing.

checklist.name: The reconciliation sentence diagnosed and rewritten
checklist.description: '`revenue_daily` reconciles with the finance team's numbers' is flagged because nothing in it says what it is compared against, so two people can run the same check and disagree about whether it passed. The replacement must name all three of a specific source of truth, the specific comparison performed, and a tolerance. Missing any of the three scores at most half. Returning 'define reconciliation' or 'agree this with finance' with no replacement wording scores zero.

checklist.name: Late-arrival sentence kept at the milder weight
checklist.description: 'Orders captured before the target day but written to `orders` after that day's run are folded into the affected day's row on a later run' is raised, but below the two sentences that cannot be checked at all — the outcome is visible and unarguable and only the input domain is absent. The replacement must supply a lateness window, which runs re-compute which days, and what happens to an order arriving outside that window. Not raising it scores zero. Giving it the same weight as the reconciliation or board-deck sentences scores at most half.

checklist.name: Reconciliation routed onward
checklist.description: Because the unusable sentence is a claim about what a warehouse model holds, the review says where it has to go next, naming the data-contract-extractor workflow as the place a reconciliation rule gets formalised into a checkable contract rather than leaving it as wording advice. Naming no onward target scores at most half; the requester said one round of Priya's attention is all he gets and needs to know what comes after it.

checklist.name: MUST NOT score the notes or the context
checklist.description: MUST NOT assess the Context paragraph about Marta's spreadsheet, the 'Risk:' note about the `orders.status` vocabulary, or the 'Open question:' about multi-currency as sentences that do or do not fall short — none of the three asserts what the model does. Any of them appearing as a row scores zero here, and the stated count of sentences assessed must exclude all three.

checklist.name: Deliverable, call and counts
checklist.description: docs/revenue-daily-review.md exists, gives a top-line call on whether the spec can go to data engineering next week, states a count of sentences assessed and a count falling short, and leaves docs/revenue-daily-spec.md unmodified. Editing the spec file scores zero here.
